newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see NTT in yen, Canada in dollars.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see NTT in yen, Canada in dollars.

text.p: Activity in the Eurobond market was brisk on Tuesday, with the main deals a 100 billion yen 10-year bond by NTT and a $1.0 billion five-year global for Canada.
NTT sparked controversy by choosing two U.S. securities firms to underwrite its deal, the first liquid Euroyen issue to surface this year.
The deal was priced at four b.p. over 194 JGBs, which bankers said was on the tight side.
"We would have liked to have seen an extra five to 10 b.p. of spread to attract investors to this corporate deal," a trader at a Japanese bank said.
"So far, the major investment funds are waiting to buy the deal until the spread widens," he said.

But lead managers Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley reported strong demand, and said they had already sold most of their bonds. An official at Morgan Stanley said the spread was unlikely to widen, and could even tighten.
Bankers elsewhere said the leads were committed to maintainig the launch spread.
In dollars, Canada's $1.0 billion five-year global bond was well-received, giving investors a rare chance to buy a liquid sovereign deal.
Bankers said the eight b.p. launch spread did not leave any room for tightening, but the deal was nevertheless well-bid.
On the emerging market side the main deals were a $200 million five-year bond for Lithuania and a $200 million three-year bond for Russian commercial bank SBS-Agro.
SBS-Agro is the first such borrower to issue a fixed-rate Eurobond -- so far supply from Russia has been restricted to sovereign and municipality issues.
First launched for $150 million, the deal was increased to $200 million during the morning session.

An official at lead manager J.P. Morgan said the deal was twice oversubscribed, which bodes well for other Russian banks eyeing the market. He said the funds were raised more cheaply than those available in the syndicated loan market.
This month alone two deals are expected -- one for Alfa-Bank and one for Uneximbank -- both of which are currently holding investor presentations in Europe.
